summary.name: Earnote
summary.one_liner: Earnote is a free, open source (MIT) Mac and iPhone app that records lectures or meetings, transcribes them locally with Whisper, and turns them into structured notes.
use_cases: Turning meeting recordings into summaries and tasks
Creating flashcards and PDF study sheets for exams
Transcribing Zoom, Teams or Meet calls on a Mac
Keeping private recordings on your own devices
summary.what_it_does: Earnote captures microphone and system audio together, shows a live transcript while recording on power, and writes a note with a summary, topics, decisions and tick-off tasks. Transcription runs locally with Whisper, and the notes are written by a language model that runs on the device, though the user can choose cloud AI providers such as Claude, OpenAI or Gemini. It can make flashcards (exportable to Anki), a PDF study sheet, and export notes to Notion, Obsidian, Logseq, Apple Notes, Bear, Craft or Markdown. A custom dictionary corrects names and terms, and clicking transcript timestamps plays back that moment.
notable: Transcription and note writing run on-device with Whisper and a local language model, with no account or API key needed
Free and MIT-licensed open source; Earnote Pro on iPhone/iPad is a one-time purchase with speaker detection, ask-your-notes and translation
Captures system audio so Zoom, Teams and Meet participants appear in the transcript
Click transcript timestamps to hear that moment and search across all recordings
caveats: Mac version requires macOS 15 or newer on Apple Silicon with about 8 GB memory; first run downloads about 1.6 GB speech model and 2.3 GB local AI
No Windows version and none planned, because it relies on Apple's speech and AI frameworks
Mac app is not on the Mac App Store; iPhone version needs iOS 26 and on-device AI needs iPhone 15 Pro or newer
Recording people without consent may be illegal depending on jurisdiction; the user is responsible
